verdict.rationale: Sentry's own docs describe event-triggered automation that runs without user involvement. Seer Autofix automatically scans incoming issues, finds root causes, automates triage, and can create PRs. Alerts take action, such as creating tickets or calling webhooks, when issues match pre-defined rules. However, the evidence covers only these specific event-triggered flows, not general user-defined background automations, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documentation of how users configure and control Seer's autonomous runs (triggers, thresholds, guardrails), any recurring or scheduled background automation as opposed to issue-triggered actions, general-purpose user-defined agent workflows, and independent or hands-on corroboration that autonomous runs work as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Automatically scan issues as they come into Sentry, finding root causes, and automating triage. PR Creation: Use Autofix to generate a code fix and create a PR.
